headline: The cookies live on Facebook. Google is still looking for a different Lilac Bakery.
summary: This is a licensed cottage kitchen, not a Main Street shop. Leslie takes orders by Facebook, text, or email, and the work is real. The home page is one sentence that sends you to Facebook. A stranger typing Lilac Bakery can land in Winnipeg or Lombard. Directories will invent hours for a door that is not a walk-in.

signals.note: Ramona people can find you on Facebook. A stranger typing Lilac Bakery does not clearly get a Ramona cottage kitchen. There is a Lilac Bakery in Winnipeg, one in Lombard, and a Lilac City Bakery in Spokane. The name is easy to love and easy to mix up.
signals.next: Keep Google as Lilac Heights Bakery in Ramona, cottage food, by order. The extra Heights word is doing work. Do not let a walk-in bakery in another state steal the pin.

signals.note: The number (760) 653-8993 and leslieannedelaney@gmail.com are consistent. Facebook, the contact page, and the listings all use them. The contact page even asks people to put Bakery in the email subject, which is honest for a home inbox.
signals.next: Keep that pair everywhere. Do not add a second number.

signals.note: The site has no hours. Facebook does not clearly post a week. Directories will invent open and closed for a kitchen that is not a walk-in shop. A neighbor who trusts Google can drive to La Plata Court expecting a counter.
signals.next: Write one line: licensed home bakery, by order, Facebook or text 653-8993, not a walk-in shop. Put that line on Google and the home page.

signals.note: The work lives on Facebook. The site says so. Public listings do not clearly show the cookies, the cakes, or the preserves. A first-time neighbor cannot see the care before they message.
signals.next: Put four current photos on Google: a cookie, a cake, a jam, and a decorated order. Facebook can keep the rest.

signals.note: lilacheightsbakery.com loads and belongs to you. The home page is one sentence: contact us, pictures are on Facebook. About and contact exist if someone hunts. Leftover WordPress.com chrome is still public. A phone visitor lands in an empty hallway.
signals.next: Three lines at the top: Ramona licensed home bakery, the phone, the order line. Then the Facebook link. That is a complete site for a cottage kitchen.

signals.note: Name is close. Phone is good. Address is a house on La Plata Court, which is true for a licensed kitchen. If Google treats it like a storefront, people drive to a door that is not staffed for walk-ins. The bigger leak is the other Lilac bakeries sharing the search.
signals.next: Keep the public name Lilac Heights Bakery, Ramona. Mark the listing as by appointment. Do not hide that it is a cottage kitchen. That honesty saves wasted trips.
